summary: Pinned model commit dropped during edge priority reordering in staged canary, causing transient rollbacks and mixed outputs
description:
Issue summary: BrightVoice AI reported intermittent flips from their pinned model (rw-infer-v2.1) back to the legacy variant during a staged canary promotion. The flips coincide with an edge priority reordering event triggered by a regional capacity rebalance.
Impact: Multiple customer sessions observed mixed outputs (some responses from rw-infer-v2.1, some from open-llama-65b-q4 legacy), session-level latency increased ~3x, and BrightVoice reported degraded quality affecting their chat product for several customer-facing sessions.
Environment: Production (BrightVoice tenant on Dedicated cluster), incidents observed in us-east and eu-west during 2026-03-10 03:20–06:00 UTC. Orchestrator version: 4.7.2-edge, Edge-proxy version: 2.13.7. Serving runtime: 1.12.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a staged canary promotion of rw-infer-v2.1 with 10% weight in eu-west and us-east. 2) Simulate a capacity rebalance: preempt a standby GPU in us-east region to force one orchestrator priority swap. 3) Send a burst of 200 tenant-scoped streaming sessions pinned to rw-infer-v2.1. 4) Observe routing headers and model variant in responses.
Observed behavior: During the orchestrator priority swap, edge-proxy queues reordered a subset of in-flight requests. Pin commit messages (control-plane -> edge commit) were delivered but not applied consistently: some edge nodes reported successful commit, others returned a 409-like response in logs and treated the commit as a no-op. Result: a window where requests for the same session hit mixed variants and some sessions fell back to the legacy variant.
Expected behavior: Pin commit should be applied atomically per-session across edge nodes or rejected in a way that preserves existing pin (no mixed-variant window).
Logs & traces:
- edge-proxy logs (us-east/edge-7): "pin_commit: id=tvk-3345 -> commit_failed: priority-mismatch-requeue"
- orchestrator trace (4.7.2-edge): "commit-broadcast delayed by 420ms for shard s72 during priority-reorder"
- serving-runtime logs: intermittent 502s during the same timeframe
Workaround taken: Immediately increased pin-commit timeout on customer's tenant to 3s and pinned at an account-level sticky token to force session affinity to a single edge node. This reduced mixed responses but did not eliminate them for long-lived streams.
Temporary mitigation: 1) Advise customer to enable tenant-level affinity override until a permanent fix is deployed. 2) Apply an emergency patch to edge-proxy to avoid reordering in-flight commit messages during priority swaps (rollbackable hotfix deployed to us-east on 2026-03-11 01:10 UTC).
Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Edge reordering combined with non-idempotent commit semantics allows a later-in-time commit to be applied on some nodes while earlier commits are dropped; this causes split-view across nodes.
- Hypothesis B: Orchestrator broadcast uses a best-effort shard fanout; priority swaps cause some shards to queue commits and apply them out-of-order relative to in-flight requests.
- Evidence: Correlated commit-broadcast timestamps show 300–600ms skew between shards. Edge nodes that reported "commit_failed: priority-mismatch-requeue" subsequently resumed normal routing once the emergency patch prevented message reordering.
Follow-up tasks created:
- INT-4421: Add idempotent compare-and-set for pin commits at the edge (planned SRV-Q2-375).
- ORCH-1290 (github PR): Ensure orchestrator commit broadcasts are ordered by commit-timestamp per-tenant.
- Add a canary test scenario to the release pipeline that simulates priority reorders while committing pins.
Customer communication: BrightVoice notified via #support-private and provided session ids and sample transcripts. We promised hourly updates until resolution.
Next steps: 1) Engineering to implement idempotent pin apply (INT-4421) and ensure commit ordering (ORCH-1290). 2) Expand edge-proxy hotfix to eu-west after validation (scheduled 2026-03-15). 3) Add observability: per-tenant commit-apply success rate metric and alert (SLO threshold 99.95%). 4) Postmortem to be written in confluence and shared with BrightVoice when complete.
Severity rationale: P1/Sev1 because pinned model behavior violated contract and produced mixed outputs for end users; impacts SLAs and quality.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start staged canary promotion of rw-infer-v2.1 at 10% weight in eu-west and us-east. 2) Trigger regional capacity rebalance to force orchestrator priority swap (simulate preempt on standby GPU). 3) Issue a burst of 200 streaming sessions pinned to rw-infer-v2.1 using BrightVoice tenant tokens. 4) Monitor edge-proxy logs for 'commit_failed: priority-mismatch-requeue' and correlate with model variant in responses.
investigation_summary: Initial triage: Support confirmed reports and collected traces. SRE reproduced message reordering during orchestrator priority swap in a staging cluster which led to inconsistent pin apply across edge shards. Engineering confirmed commit broadcast is not strictly ordered and pin apply is not idempotent, allowing split-state under concurrent priority reorders. Emergency mitigation reduced occurrence but permanent fixes require adding idempotent compare-and-set and stronger ordering guarantees from orchestrator.
resolution_notes: Workarounds: tenant-level affinity override and increased pin-commit timeout reduced customer impact. Hotfix prevented message reordering on us-east and decreased incident frequency. Permanent fix: engineering to implement idempotent pin apply and ordered commit broadcasts (target release 4.8.0). Customer-facing timeline: planned eu-west hotfix 2026-03-15 and full rollout of fixes in 4.8.0 (canary + staged rollout) by end of March. Postmortem owner: Liam Chen.
